question.text: Two discs of same mass and different radii are made of different materials such that their thicknesses are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> respectively. The densities of materials are in the ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>:</mo><mn>5</mn></math>. The moment of inertia of these discs respectively about their diameters will be in the ratio of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mn>6</mn></mfrac></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is ______.

solution.text:
Mass of the disc in terms of density can be written as, m=ρπR2t.

⇒R2=mρπt

Now moment of inertia of the disc about the diameter is, mR24.

Therefore,

I=mR24=m24ρπt⇒I∝1ρt

Required ratio, I1I2=ρ2t2ρ1t1=53×0.51=56

Hence, x=5.
